blocks.text: K-Help: Korea Life Platform for Foreign Residents
Comprehensive Architectural Blueprint, Delivered Milestones (V1–V8), & Future Roadmap
Authors: NP Coders Engineering Team | Date: September 2026 | Repository: D:\NP-CODERS\K-Help

Foreign residents in South Korea (international students, professional visa holders, migrant workers, and marriage migrants) encounter systemic structural friction. Critical daily living needs—such as obtaining Alien Registration Cards (ARC), navigating National Health Insurance (NHIS), opening bank accounts, finding non-discriminatory housing with transparent wolse/jeonse deposits, securing legal employment, and drafting polite Korean messages for landlords—are fragmented across separate government portals and Korean-only apps.

K-Help consolidates these fragmented domains into a unified, reliable, dual-stack platform built on Next.js 16 (App Router + Tailwind CSS 4) and Spring Boot 3.4 (Java 21 + PostgreSQL 15 + Redis 7 + WebSocket/STOMP).

blocks.text: 5. Strategic Recommendations: Making K-Help More Natural & Working
To elevate K-Help from a feature-complete academic project into an organic, indispensable daily tool for foreign residents, we recommend prioritizing these 5 pragmatic enhancements:

items: Contextual 'Direct Contact' Bridges: Connect listings directly to Chat. Clicking 'Message Landlord' on a housing listing or 'Inquire' on a job post should instantly launch a 1:1 chat pre-populated with reference details.

Inline AI Polite Message Assistant: In the chat and comment boxes, provide a one-click 'Make Polite' button. A foreigner typing informal English or blunt Korean can instantly convert their message into respectful Korean honorifics before hitting send.

Seed realistic community conversations and housing/job photos: Populate 15-20 active community discussions with realistic Q&As (e.g. 'Can I work 20 hours on D-2 visa?') and high-quality room photos to make the platform feel lively.
Real-time Desktop Notification Badges: Add an unread message indicator dot on the top navbar that updates via WebSocket when another user sends a chat message.

Live LLM API Integration: Replace the mock AI regex pipeline with OpenAI GPT-4o-mini or Claude 3.5 Haiku using environment variable keys (OPENAI_API_KEY) in application.properties for fluid translation and contract analysis.
